description: Engine represents an instance of a Web Application Firewall (WAF) engine.

apiVersion.description:
APIVersion defines the versioned schema of this representation of an object.
Servers should convert recognized schemas to the latest internal value, and
may reject unrecognized values.
More info: https://git.k8s.io/community/contributors/devel/sig-architecture/api-conventions.md#resources

kind.description:
Kind is a string value representing the REST resource this object represents.
Servers may infer this from the endpoint the client submits requests to.
Cannot be updated.
In CamelCase.
More info: https://git.k8s.io/community/contributors/devel/sig-architecture/api-conventions.md#types-kinds

spec.description: spec defines the desired state of Engine.

driver.description:
driver configures the mechanism used to deploy the WAF filter into the
target workload. When omitted, the operator uses a default driver for the
underlying Engine (eg.: WASM for Istio)

type.description: type selects the driver mechanism used to deploy the WAF filter.

wasm.description: wasm contains configuration specific to the WASM driver.

sha256.description:
sha256 is the lowercase hexadecimal SHA-256 of the raw WASM bytes
served at url. It must be set together with url.

url.description:
url is an HTTPS URL serving raw WASM bytes. It must be set together
with sha256. When both url and sha256 are omitted, the operator uses its
bundled module.

x-kubernetes-validations.message: url and sha256 must be set together; omit both to use the bundled module
url must be an https URL without userinfo, query, or fragment
sha256 must be 64 lowercase hexadecimal characters
wasm config is required when type is wasm

failurePolicy.description:
failurePolicy determines the behavior when the WAF is not ready or
encounters errors. Valid values are:

- "Fail": Block traffic when the WAF is not ready or encounters errors
- "Allow": Allow traffic through when the WAF is not ready or encounters errors

When omitted, this means the user has no opinion and the platform
will choose a reasonable default, which is subject to change over time.

The current default is fail.

observability.description:
observability configures WAF dataplane observability independently of the
driver used to deploy the Engine. The operator translates this intent into
driver-specific settings.

mode.description:
mode controls whether WAF dataplane telemetry is available to the target
platform's observability pipeline.

ruleSet.description:
ruleSet specifies the RuleSet resource that will be used to load rules
into the Engine. The referenced RuleSet must be in the same namespace
as the Engine.

name.description: name is the name of the RuleSet in the same namespace as the Engine.

ruleSetCacheServer.description:
ruleSetCacheServer is deprecated and ignored. The operator distributes
rules through ECDS and does not start the legacy HTTP rule server, so
this field has no effect.

pollIntervalSeconds.description:
pollIntervalSeconds specifies how often the WAF should check for
configuration updates. The value is specified in seconds.

When omitted, this means the user has no opinion and the platform
will choose a reasonable default, which is subject to change over time.
The current default is 15 seconds.

target.description:
target identifies the workload that the Engine protects. The operator
derives the workload selector from this reference (e.g., for Gateway
targets, the GEP-1762 gateway-name label is used).

name.description:
name is the name of the target resource in the same namespace as the
Engine. For Gateway targets, the operator derives the workload selector
from this name using the GEP-1762 convention
(gateway.networking.k8s.io/gateway-name label).

Must conform to RFC 1035 label syntax: lowercase alphanumeric or
hyphens, must start with a letter and end with an alphanumeric
(e.g. "my-gateway", "gw1"). This matches Kubernetes Service naming
rules and ensures compatibility with Gateway implementations that
derive Service names from the Gateway name.

x-kubernetes-validations.message: name must be a valid DNS-1035 label (lowercase, starts with a letter)

provider.description:
provider identifies the infrastructure provider that manages the
target workload. The provider determines which driver types are
valid for the Engine.

This field is immutable after creation. Changing providers requires
creating a new Engine resource so the controller does not need to
clean up and recreate child resources from the previous driver.

Currently supported providers and their allowed driver types:
- "Istio": supports "wasm" driver type.

Future providers may support different driver types. For example,
"EnvoyGateway" will only support "dynamicModule" once implemented.

When omitted, this means the user has no opinion and the platform
will choose a reasonable default, which is subject to change over time.

The current default is Istio.

type.description:
type is the type of resource being targeted.

Currently only supports "Gateway" mode, utilizing Gateway API resources.

x-kubernetes-validations.message: field provider is immutable once set
name is required when type is Gateway
provider "Istio" is only supported when target type is Gateway
driver type must be compatible with the target provider (Istio supports wasm)

status.description: status defines the observed state of Engine.

acceptedConfiguration.description:
acceptedConfiguration records the last accepted complete Engine
configuration. It survives desired-input degradation and is not a payload
store.

binaryURL.description:
binaryURL is the URL of the raw WASM binary used by the accepted
configuration.

driverType.description:
driverType is the resolved driver type of the accepted configuration.
Publication requires it; records written before this field existed
mismatch and wait for re-acceptance.

emptyRulesPolicy.description:
emptyRulesPolicy is the resolved empty-rules policy of the accepted
configuration. Publication requires it; records written before this
field existed mismatch and wait for re-acceptance.

failurePolicy.description: failurePolicy is the failure policy of the accepted configuration.

filterStateLogs.description:
filterStateLogs reports whether the accepted configuration renders WAF
filter-state logging. Publication requires it; records written before
this field existed mismatch and wait for re-acceptance.

observedGeneration.description:
observedGeneration is the Engine generation whose configuration was
accepted.

renderingSchemaVersion.description:
renderingSchemaVersion is the schema version of the rendered runtime
configuration.

ruleSetContentHash.description:
ruleSetContentHash is the accepted RuleSet content hash, in the form
sha256:<64 lowercase hexadecimal characters>.

ruleSetUID.description: ruleSetUID is the UID of the RuleSet used for the accepted configuration.

version.description:
version is the content-addressed version of the accepted configuration,
in the form sha256:<64 lowercase hexadecimal characters>.

vm.description:
vm records the resolved WASM VM settings of the accepted configuration.
Publication requires it; records written before this field existed
mismatch and wait for re-acceptance.

codeTimeout.description:
codeTimeout is the resolved WASM code fetch and execution timeout of
the accepted configuration, as a Go duration string (for example
"10s").

runtime.description: runtime is the resolved WASM runtime of the accepted configuration.

vmID.description: vmID is the resolved WASM VM ID of the accepted configuration.

wasmSHA256.description:
wasmSHA256 is the lowercase hexadecimal SHA-256 of the WASM binary used
by the accepted configuration.

conditions.description:
conditions represent the current state of the Engine resource.
Each condition has a unique type and reflects the status of a specific
aspect of the resource.

Standard condition types include:
- "Accepted": the target is valid and not contested by another Engine.
   Reasons: "Accepted", "TargetNotFound", "TargetConflict"
- "Ready": the engine has been successfully deployed and is operational
- "Progressing": the resource is being created or updated
- "Degraded": the resource failed to reach or maintain its desired state
- "ObservabilityReady": optional Telemetry was created and is available

The status of each condition is one of True, False, or Unknown.

items.description: Condition contains details for one aspect of the current state of this API Resource.

lastTransitionTime.description:
lastTransitionTime is the last time the condition transitioned from one status to another.
This should be when the underlying condition changed.  If that is not known, then using the time when the API field changed is acceptable.

message.description:
message is a human readable message indicating details about the transition.
This may be an empty string.

observedGeneration.description:
observedGeneration represents the .metadata.generation that the condition was set based upon.
For instance, if .metadata.generation is currently 12, but the .status.conditions[x].observedGeneration is 9, the condition is out of date
with respect to the current state of the instance.

reason.description:
reason contains a programmatic identifier indicating the reason for the condition's last transition.
Producers of specific condition types may define expected values and meanings for this field,
and whether the values are considered a guaranteed API.
The value should be a CamelCase string.
This field may not be empty.

status.description: status of the condition, one of True, False, Unknown.

type.description: type of condition in CamelCase or in foo.example.com/CamelCase.
